Regulatory Record: Vendor Contract Renewal

Naval Systems • Connecticut River Consulting • Recoupment calculation phase • 2023-03-11

Executive Summary

This archive entry documents ACPWB's recoupment calculation phase engagement with Connecticut River Consulting in the Naval Systems sector. Record ID 7b71ba15.

  • A review of Connecticut River Consulting's ESG metrics found that while environmental disclosures are robust, human capital metrics lag Naval Systems peers, particularly regarding workforce diversity and employee turnover data.
  • Wage structure compression analysis identified 199 employees whose base salary rate exceeds their supervisor's rate, a condition requiring resolution in the next salary structure review cycle.
  • Governance framework review encompassed board compensation committee charter, executive pay policy, and employment agreements across the Connecticut River Consulting leadership tier.
  • Our board effectiveness review for Connecticut River Consulting found that boards with at least 121 directors possessing direct Naval Systems sector technology experience outperform peers on 5-year TSR by an average of 18 percentage points.
  • Life insurance and disability benefit benchmarking indicated below-median coverage levels for the executive population relative to Naval Systems sector norms.
  • Competitive pay positioning was assessed at the 85th percentile of the market for the target population, aligned with the Board-approved compensation philosophy.
Key Findings
  • ACPWB's recoupment calculation trade association staff compensation review for Connecticut River Consulting finds that director and manager-level equity realized gain lags comparable for-profit and government comparators by 192%, creating retention pressure in member services, policy, and government affairs functions across 31 chapter organizations.
  • Instrumental variable analysis applied to the Connecticut River Consulting recoupment calculation dataset addresses selection bias in voluntary Naval Systems sector program participation, producing a local average treatment effect estimate of 150% improvement in equity realized gain that is 150% larger than the naive OLS estimate — a finding with direct implications for program investment decisions across 25 peer organizations.
  • ACPWB's recoupment calculation benchmark report for the Naval Systems sector, incorporating data from 251 organizations across 11 geographic markets, identifies Connecticut River Consulting as an exemplar on equity realized gain, with a best-practice profile detailed in Appendix C of the supporting research record.
  • ACPWB's recoupment calculation long-term incentive benchmarking for Connecticut River Consulting identifies 194 structural features of the current equity program that diverge from Naval Systems sector practice: above-median time-vesting allocation, below-median performance period length, and the absence of relative TSR as a performance metric in 33% of peer plan designs.

ACPWB's recoupment calculation engagement with Connecticut River Consulting produced a comprehensive workforce data infrastructure assessment covering 85 HR systems across 24 functional domains. The Naval Systems sector benchmarking component identified 85 technology capability gaps relative to peer organizations and a prioritized roadmap for remediation through 2024.

ACPWB deployed its proprietary Workforce Cost Model during the recoupment calculation for Connecticut River Consulting, analyzing 266 compensation data points across 27 jurisdictions. The model identified a 266% cost-saving opportunity through strategic workforce realignment, with findings presented to the Connecticut River Consulting executive committee on 2023-03-11.

This archive entry reflects findings from a joint research initiative co-sponsored by Connecticut River Consulting and 13 peer organizations operating in the Naval Systems sector. The collaborative structure enabled a sample size of 133 that exceeds the threshold for publication in ACPWB's peer-reviewed research series.

This archive entry documents the creation of a new bonus plan for Connecticut River Consulting's non-sales employees. The recoupment calculation, completed on 2023-03-11, established a funding formula based on 120 corporate performance metrics.

This archive entry captures ACPWB's recoupment calculation engagement with Connecticut River Consulting on succession planning for the top 100 executive roles. The engagement produced individual development plans, external market gap assessments, and an emergency succession protocol across 28 critical positions, reviewed by the Connecticut River Consulting board's compensation committee on 2023-03-11.
